clue.text: Buzzer's high-pitched sound, quietly ignored by beadle

indicators.note: placed by, i.e. alongside, the beadle's name

parts.note: Mr Bumble is the pompous parish beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so this letter is dropped from the sound

parts.note: a beep is a short high-pitched electronic sound
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: An insect's whine is so faint that a church official doesn't notice it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Buzzer stands for 'is'. 'ignored' removes P from BEEP to leave BEE, which sits by BUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large furry bee is named for its loud droning hum, so it is a natural buzzer.

clue.text: Fundamental, thus to support rise of upper classes

indicators.note: in a down entry, the support goes beneath what it holds up
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in British market-research classification
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A declaration that something is essential for keeping the upper classes on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A and B are British social grades; 'rise of' turns them to BA in the down entry, and 'to support' puts SIC beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is at the root of a matter, so it is fundamental; plain synonym.

clue.text: Position of noble son settled in large tent

indicators.note: the son and the settling are placed inside the tent

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent used for weddings and fairs
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
sat, as in settled down on a seat

explanation.surface: A nobleman's boy has made himself at home inside a big tent.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank or territory held by a marquess, a nobleman below a duke, is that title's position.

clue.text: Seafood bishop fed to confused monarch

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so the bishop's letter goes into the others

parts.note: lost, as in bewildered
B is the chess notation for bishop
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A bewildered king or queen is offered a churchman as a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This clawed crustacean is a classic and expensive shellfish dish.

clue.text: Least extensive celebration in Berlin, starting with cheese

indicators.note: the German party begins with the cheese, so the cheese comes first

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
Fest is the German word for a festival or party

explanation.surface: A German party whose opening course is cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The briefest thing is the shortest, so it is the least extensive in length or duration.

clue.text: Forcefully acquire gold held by former abstainer

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the gold is gripped inside the other letters

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A one-time teetotaller is holding gold, perhaps obtained by threats.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, and TT (teetotal) is crossword shorthand for a non-drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain money or a promise by force or threats, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Model backed by a fabulous writer

indicators.note: backed means the word is read from back to front

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A model is supported financially by an amazing author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means writing fables, not merely wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famed for his fables, such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: A contemptible person at Oxford initially, notedly restless

parts.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sneering account of an unpleasant fellow in his first days at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, this Italian direction tells the player to perform in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Individual forks out pounds for old French coin

indicators.note: the pounds are pulled out, removed from the word; the run of letters across these two words is a coincidence, not the setter's device

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in not a soul was there
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Someone pays out money in exchange for a historical French coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forks out' looks like paying, but it removes L from SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a French coin of low value, worth a twentieth of a livre, now obsolete.

clue.text: One in lofty position astride heavy horse

parts.note: a percher is something that perches up high
on, as in sitting on a horse

explanation.surface: Someone sits high up astride a big horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a powerful French breed of draught horse, a large working animal.

clue.text: Cancel regular payment, getting round creditor

indicators.note: the payment wraps around the creditor's letters

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, paid regularly
CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor or credit

explanation.surface: Stopping a standing order once the lender has been persuaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informally to call it off or abandon it.

clue.text: Conspirator, one causing fascination?

definitions.meaning: a plotter who schemes in secret
to intrigue is to fascinate, so this is one who arouses curiosity; the question mark flags the unusual sense

explanation.surface: A schemer who is also oddly captivating.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun from the verb meaning both to plot and to arouse interest serves both senses.

clue.text: Part of Ulster a gouty Frenchman recollected

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered up again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Frenchman suffering from gout remembered a corner of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering, but read as re-collected it shuffles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, within the historic province of Ulster.

clue.text: Members of High Court live over it, surrounded by attendants

parts.note: are, as in exist
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the it is placed inside the attendants

parts.note: pages are young attendants, at court or a wedding

explanation.surface: Royal servants surround something living above them in a court.
explanation.definitionFit: These were members of the Areopagus, the high council and court of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Emphasis placed on police officer's affliction

indicators.note: the emphasis is placed after, on, the officer's letters

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
stress is emphasis on a word or point

explanation.surface: A detective's suffering made worse by being put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on officer is 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or anguish, a close synonym for affliction.

clue.text: Hesitantly name tinker with evidence of debt

parts.note: to dub is to name or give a title
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: Uncertainly calling a mender of pots by name while he holds a debt note.
explanation.walkthrough: The tinker is Christopher Sly from The Taming of the Shrew; 'with' only joins the pieces, which run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting doubtfully or uncertainly is acting hesitantly, an adverb for an adverb.

clue.text: Show-off taking problem round university

indicators.note: the problem goes round the university letter

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A braggart is presenting a puzzle around campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur affects attitudes to impress others, so is a show-off.

clue.text: Hermit's tedious task, filling a set of books

indicators.note: the task fills the space between the other letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a chore is a dull routine job

explanation.surface: A recluse has a dull job stuffing books.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on Hermit is 'is'. CHORE goes between the N and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoret, or anchorite, is a religious recluse living in seclusion, a hermit.

clue.text: Return of fantastic regiment protecting one part of Nigeria

indicators.note: the reversed word and the regiment wrap around the one
return means the word comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, fantastic
I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: A splendid regiment comes back to guard someone in a region of Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' makes BAF; I goes after its B, then RA.
explanation.definitionFit: This south-eastern region of Nigeria declared itself independent in 1967, leading to civil war.

clue.text: German four in broadcast going over French holiday region

indicators.note: the German number is placed inside
in a down clue, going over means turning back to front

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
vier is the German word for four

explanation.surface: A German quartet on air travel to the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'going over' reads the broadcast word upwards, giving RIA, which holds the German number.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coast of south-east France, a famous resort area.

clue.text: Support from beneath, needing identification

parts.note: under means beneath
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: Holding something up from below calls for proof of who you are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support from beneath' looks like the full definition, but beneath is UNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpin a structure or argument is to support or strengthen it from below.

clue.text: Raise tax invested in European shelter

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Raising a tax and putting it into a European shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: LEE is the sheltered side, away from the wind, a sailing term.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift or raise something to a higher position.

clue.text: Judge in Pennsylvania with second-class house

indicators.note: the grade comes with, next to, the rest
the judge is placed inside the state's letters

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation of the US state
a ref, referee, judges a game
B denotes second class or grade

explanation.surface: A judge living in Pennsylvania in a second-rate home.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, assembled from factory-made sections.

clue.text: Reportedly talked round those having a row? That makes you merry!

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as spoken, sounding the same

parts.note: won over means persuaded or talked round
the eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Persuading a rowing crew, hinted at being a cheering thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a row' means rowing a boat, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for one drink too many describes being slightly drunk, so it makes you merry.

clue.text: Heavyweight finally driving a two-wheeled vehicle

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A heavy load finally driving a little cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India.

clue.text: Second medal for one replacing old tree

parts.note: silver is the medal for second place

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word for

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A runner-up's medal swapped for an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a conifer with silvery undersides to its needles, a type of evergreen.

clue.text: Reportedly be short of 100,000 rupees

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, sounding alike

parts.note: to lack is to be short of

explanation.surface: Supposedly someone is short of a large sum in Indian money.
explanation.definitionFit: A lac, or lakh, is the South Asian term for one hundred thousand, especially of rupees.

clue.text: Suit Italian leader abandoned for old jacket

indicators.note: abandoned means removed, left out

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A suit whose Italian boss has gone is replaced with an old jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: An acton was a padded jacket worn under armour in medieval times.

clue.text: Brief expression of contempt about a Mexican plant

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: yuck is an exclamation of disgust
ca is circa, about

explanation.surface: A short sneering remark about a Mexican plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant native to Mexico and the American south-west.

clue.text: Short article by cricketer in London area

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
terse means short, curt
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper piece about a cricketer in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short article' looks like a newspaper item, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district of south London, home to its famous power station and dogs' home.
